history.summary: The Langaleswar Temple is an ancient Shiva shrine at Langaleswar village, Baliapal tehsil, Balasore district. The name 'Langaleswar' comes from 'langala' (plough): legend says Lord Shiva Himself ploughed the nearby paddy fields, and a plough is preserved in his memory, with hundreds of pilgrims gathering to worship Lord Langaleswar - the 'Lord of the plough' and patron deity of farmers. Local accounts (onefivenine.com) say Shiva last rested at Langaleswar, and the temple stands by the side of river Parvati (per odikala), giving it scenic beauty. The architecture is Kalinga style with a curvilinear deul. The nearest railhead is Basta; the temple is about 45-46 km east of Balasore by motorable road. CSV town correction: the temple is NOT in Balasore town - it is at Langaleswar village in Baliapal block, ~45 km east of the district HQ. Identity is moderately supported by Odisha tourism and village sources but the temple's antiquity and builder are unverified; do not confuse with the unrelated Langaleswar temple at Cuttack. No verified image could be found after genuine searching (image results were of other temples, e.g. Varanasi's Lankeshwar) - media left empty.

town_description: Langaleswar is a village in Baliapal tehsil, Baleshwar district, Odisha, in the coastal plain near the Bay of Bengal (rivers Budhabalanga and Subarnarekha nearby), about 45 km east of Balasore town. It is known for its ancient Shiva temple of the plough legend.
